linkage_keys_or_join_strategy: MEASURE_ID; BREAKDOWN with PRIMARY_LEVEL and SECONDARY_LEVEL; REPORTING_PERIOD_END; ODS provider code (joins to DS068)
minimum_metadata_to_capture: source version/release; query/filter; retrieval timestamp; licence/approval; file/API response hash; field/codebook version; transformation log
quality_checks: coverage; missingness; duplicates; definition drift; temporal completeness; provenance; dependency; representativeness; disclosure risk
major_limitations: CARRIES NO GENDER-SERVICE, GENDER-DYSPHORIA OR GENDER-IDENTITY-CLINIC REFERRAL MEASURE: all 121 England-level measures in the June 2026 archive were scanned and none exists, because gender services are commissioned outside this collection. The 'England; Gender' breakdown is the PATIENT'S RECORDED GENDER applied to general mental health activity and is not a gender-service referral count. PROVIDER COVERAGE RAMPS ~4.6x ACROSS THE SERIES (about 91 submitting providers in 2016 against about 420 in 2026) while the England headline roughly doubles, so an early-year rise may be ascertainment rather than incidence and the connector carries coverage per month beside every series. MHS32 is published under one measure id as BOTH a monthly and a rolling three-month total sharing an end date, so selecting on the end date alone mixes windows differing by a factor of three. REPORTING_PERIOD_START uses month-first in the 2016-2023 file and day-first later, so only the month-end date can be trusted to date a row. MHS01 was renamed midway ('People in contact with services' to 'People with an open referral'), so the measure id and not the name pins a stratum. England-level MHS32 begins only in April 2022; the full Apr-2016 span exists only for MHS01, and the two are a flow and a stock and must not be spliced. Suppressed cells are written '*' and are MISSING, never zero. Aggregate counts only, no microdata.
current_status: Live and streamed from local files by oslt_research.connectors.mhsds_local, which performs no network access; England MHS01 verified complete for all 123 months Apr 2016 to Jun 2026 with no gaps and no duplicates. Distinct from DS068, which indexes NHS England publication files without fetching them.
